newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RESULTS TODAY--SISTER FIRMS TO BOOST ANGLO .
newsitem.headline: RESULTS TODAY--SISTER FIRMS TO BOOST ANGLO .

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa will harvest wealthy profits from its sister companies De Beers Consolidated and Minorco SA to grow its year earnings by about 27 percent, analysts said.
Anglo results are due at 1400 GMT on Tuesday.

Analysts polled by Reuters forecast a consensus headline earnings per share figure of 2,220.5 cents compared to the previous year's 1,743 cents. Their numbers lay within a range of 2,165 and 2,294 cents.
They forecast a consensus dividend of 690 cents per share within a range of 680 cents to 700 cents and compared to 570 cents previously.
"I think they're going to be particularly good," said Robynn Kearney at Barnard, Jacobs, Mellet and Co.
But analysts said the current financial year did not present as glowing a picture with earnings from gold operations likely to be much diminished because of the dismal bullion price.
Rich profits from both diamond giant De Beers and offshore arm Minorco would contribute greatly to Anglo's earnings.
"De Beers was very good. It (the rise) will really be on De Beers. Minorco was also up," Kearney said.

Announcing year results in March, De Beers declared a dazzling $1,344 million year profit, up from $986 million previously. Also in March, Minorco jumped its year net income nine percent to $396.4 million.

But analysts said calculations could only rely on companies that have already reported and that profits from unlisted subsidiaries and exceptional items could throw a spanner in the works, either adding to or taking away from expectations.

"We know about Amcoal, De Beers, Minorco. But what we don't know about are the funnies. It's what they bring to account by way of exceptionals and subsidiaries that can skew results," said an anlayst who asked not to be identified.
Earnings would also be helped by the rand's depreciation over the last year, but analysts said its current firmer leaning would be one of the reasons behind smaller profits in the current year.

"There's the rand factor, too. A year ago the rand had not depreciated fully. But in 1998 we won't have the depreciation and it could could even strengthen. That wouldn't be good for Anglo because they're mostly commodity based," Kearney said.
Analysts said that Anglo's earnings for the 1997/98 financial year would be fairly flat, possibly rising 10 percent.
The current feeble bullion price would also likely take its toll on Anglo this year with gold mines already looking dismal.
Available profit for Anglo's gold mines decreased 34 percent in the quarter to end-March to 224.3 million rand.
